title: BigQuery Audit and Cost

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.7 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.7 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="bigquery.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="jobservice.jobcompleted"

| sort -_time
description: BigQuery can generate massive costs from poorly optimized queries. Audit and cost tracking prevents bill shock and identifies optimization opportunities.
value: Detecting bigquery audit and cost early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Forward BigQuery audit logs via Pub/Sub. Calculate cost from billed bytes ($5/TB). Create dashboard showing cost per user, top expensive queries, and slot utilization.
visualization: Table (user, queries, cost), Bar chart (top costly queries), Trend line (daily cost).

| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward BigQuery audit logs via Pub/Sub. Calculate cost from billed bytes ($5/TB). Create dashboard showing cost per user, top expensive queries, and slot utilization.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="bigquery.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="jobservice.jobcompleted"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.7_bigquery_audit_and_cost_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect bigquery audit and cost. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_7_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, queries, cost), Bar chart (top costly queries), Trend line (daily cost)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of bigquery audit and cost so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
